name: Eliel
overview: Eliel was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as an overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah. His role involved responsibility for sacred duties within the Levitical service, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:13. No additional personal notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliel means 'G-d is my G-d,' reflecting a declaration of faith and devotion. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant theological meaning in Hebrew, emphasizing the believer's relationship with God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Eliel as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Eliel's significance lies in his administrative role over the consecrated things, highlighting the organized and sacred nature of Levitical duties during the time of King Hezekiah's reforms. His service under Conaniah underscores the importance of faithful stewardship in the worship and maintenance of the temple, reflecting a Christ-centered model of dedicated service to God.
